encounters.cc: Perineal pain and sensation of incomplete bowel evacuation immediately following vaginal delivery with episiotomy

lines: Perineal pain and sensation of incomplete bowel evacuation immediately following vaginal delivery with episiotomy
Undergoes spontaneous vaginal delivery at 39 weeks gestation.
Due to concern about shoulder dystocia during the second stage of labor, a midline episiotomy is performed to widen the vaginal outlet.
The delivery is otherwise uncomplicated, and a healthy newborn is delivered with good Apgar scores.
- Mother: Postpartum depression following second pregnancy
Postpartum examination reveals a clean surgical extension of the perineal incision and no vaginal lacerations.
On examination, the perineal incision is intact, but there is decreased anal sphincter tone and minimal voluntary contraction with digital rectal exam.
No visible mucosal lacerations are seen.
There is no evidence of rectovaginal fistula.
The remainder of the pelvic exam is normal, and the uterus is firm and well-contracted.

encounters.cc: Routine postpartum visit with tearfulness, irritability, and difficulty sleeping 10 days after delivery

lines: Routine postpartum visit with tearfulness, irritability, and difficulty sleeping 10 days after delivery
The patient returns for routine postpartum evaluation approximately 10 days following vaginal delivery with episiotomy complicated by external anal sphincter injury.
She gave birth to a healthy baby girl 10 days ago and reports feeling overwhelmed and tearful since delivery, with episodes of unexplained crying and irritability.
She also mentions difficulty sleeping and concentrating, which she attributes to the new responsibilities of motherhood.
She denies any thoughts of harming herself or her baby.
- Mother: Postpartum depression following second pregnancy
Her complete blood count and thyroid function tests are within normal limits.

encounters.cc: Persistent localized pain at the base of the spine for two weeks, exacerbated by sitting, following vaginal delivery three weeks ago

lines: Persistent localized pain at the base of the spine for two weeks, exacerbated by sitting, following vaginal delivery three weeks ago
The patient returns for evaluation of persistent pain three weeks following her vaginal delivery, with recent history of external anal sphincter injury and postpartum blues.
She reports that the pain is localized at the base of her spine and is exacerbated by sitting down or transitioning from sitting to standing.
She denies any recent trauma or injury to the area.
She gave birth to her first child via vaginal delivery three weeks ago.
The delivery was complicated by a prolonged second stage of labor.
She is not taking any medications
- Mother: Postpartum depression following second pregnancy
On physical examination, there is tenderness to palpation over the coccyx.
No overlying skin changes or masses are noted.
Rectal examination is deferred due to patient discomfort.

encounters.cc: Involuntary urinary leakage with coughing or laughing for four weeks since vaginal delivery

lines: Involuntary urinary leakage with coughing or laughing for four weeks since vaginal delivery
The patient returns to the obstetrics clinic for further evaluation of postpartum symptoms following vaginal delivery complicated by external anal sphincter injury and recent coccydynia.
She gave birth to a healthy baby girl vaginally 4 weeks ago.
She reports that since the delivery, she has experienced involuntary leakage of urine when she coughs or laughs.
She denies any burning with urination or increased frequency.
- Mother: Postpartum depression following second pregnancy
On physical examination, there is no evidence of urinary tract infection or pelvic organ prolapse.
A cough stress test is positive for urine leakage.

encounters.cc: Routine 6-week postpartum visit with persistent feelings of hopelessness, guilt, and anhedonia

lines: Routine 6-week postpartum visit with persistent feelings of hopelessness, guilt, and anhedonia

The patient returns for her routine six-week postpartum visit following vaginal delivery complicated by external anal sphincter injury, having previously presented with postpartum blues and ongoing pelvic floor dysfunction including coccydynia and stress urinary incontinence.
She reports feeling "down" and "hopeless" most days since the delivery, with difficulty sleeping even when her baby is asleep.
She admits to having little interest in activities she used to enjoy and feels overwhelmed and guilty about not being a good mother.
She has difficulty concentrating and making decisions, and her appetite has decreased significantly.
She tearfully confesses that she has had thoughts of harming herself but has not made any plans.
She denies any thoughts of harming her baby.
She had an uncomplicated pregnancy and vaginal delivery.
- Mother: Postpartum depression following second pregnancy

encounters.cc: Six-week history of fecal incontinence and malodorous tan-brown vaginal discharge with gas bubbles

lines: Six-week history of fecal incontinence and malodorous tan-brown vaginal discharge with gas bubbles
She returns postpartum with sphincter injury.
She reports that the discharge is tan-brown and occasionally contains gas bubbles.
She gave birth to her first child vaginally 8 weeks ago and sustained a fourth-degree perineal laceration, which was repaired immediately postpartum.
- Mother: Postpartum depression following second pregnancy
Vital signs are within normal limits.
On examination, the patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress.
Pelvic examination reveals a small amount of tan-brown discharge in the vaginal vault and a dark red, velvety area of tissue on the posterior vaginal wall.
No masses are palpable, and the remainder of the pelvic examination is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Acute difficulty walking and numbness over the anteromedial thigh 24 hours after vaginal delivery

lines: Acute difficulty walking and numbness over the anteromedial thigh 24 hours after vaginal delivery

The multiparous patient with history of prior sphincter injury and fistula is 24 hours postpartum following vaginal delivery of a healthy baby boy complicated by prolonged second stage of labor requiring hyperflexion of her hips.
- Mother: Postpartum depression following second pregnancy
On physical examination, she has a decreased sensation over the anteromedial aspect of her right thigh and weakness during hip flexion and knee extension on the same side.
Deep tendon reflexes are normal, and there is no back pain or tenderness.

encounters.cc: Routine 6-week postpartum visit with low mood, sleep disturbance, and irritability

lines: Routine 6-week postpartum visit with low mood, sleep disturbance, and irritability

The patient is a 37-year-old female returning for her routine 6-week postpartum visit following a delivery complicated by femoral nerve neuropathy, with a history of postpartum depression after her 2020 delivery.
She reports feeling "down" and has trouble sleeping, even when her baby is asleep.
She expresses concern about her lack of interest in activities she used to enjoy and admits to feeling overwhelmed and irritable.
She denies any thoughts of harming herself or her baby.
Her pregnancy was uncomplicated, and she has no prior history of psychiatric illness.
- Mother: Postpartum depression following second pregnancy
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On examination, she appears fatigued but is otherwise well-appearing.
The physician decides to screen for postpartum depression.
